questions: Did your difficulty walking begin suddenly, within hours or a few days?
Have you had any new weakness on one side of your body?
Have you had facial drooping, trouble speaking, or sudden vision loss?
Have you recently fallen or injured your back, hips, or legs?
Are you having severe or worsening back pain?
Do you have numbness or tingling in your legs?
Do you have numbness around your groin or buttocks?
Have you recently lost control of your bladder or bowels?
Is one leg painful or swollen?
Does walking cause pain in your legs that improves when you sit or rest?
Do you have pain shooting from your back into either leg?
Have you felt dizzy or as though you might faint?
Have you actually fainted recently?
Are you having chest pain or shortness of breath?
Do you have pain in your hips, knees, or feet when walking?
Has this problem been gradually worsening over weeks or months?
Have you had tremors, stiffness, or slowed movements?
Have you had fever, unexplained weight loss, or unusual fatigue?
Have you started any new medications recently?
Have you had similar walking problems in the past?

results: 1. Comprehensive neurological examination, including gait, stride length, arm swing, turning, rigidity, bradykinesia, tremor, postural stability, and cerebellar testing
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
walking backward: the slow, guarded, wide-based pattern PERSISTS
running: cannot run; the pattern does not normalise
observation for excessive slowness or uneconomic posture: deliberately slow and broad-based; lumbar hyperlordosis is LACKING in this patient
muscle tone (spasticity, rigidity, paratonia): genuine axial and lower-limb rigidity on passive movement
finger-tapping for bradykinesia and decrement: no decrement
MRC power in all four limbs: 5/5 throughout
sensory examination (including midline splitting, allodynia): normal
3. Review of all current and prior medications for dopamine-blocking or parkinsonism-inducing drugs
4. Brain MRI without and with contrast
5. Complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, thyroid-stimulating hormone, vitamin B12, and folate levels
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
full blood count, renal and liver profile: normal
7. Dopamine-transporter SPECT (DaTscan) if the clinical examination remains diagnostically uncertain
DaTSCAN (dopamine transporter SPECT): normal tracer uptake
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional neurological symptom disorder presenting as a functional gait disorder (functional parkinsonian gait), with no evidence of structural or degenerative nigrostriatal disease

ALTERNATIVE 1: Stiff-person spectrum disorder

ALTERNATIVE 2: Early atypical parkinsonism, particularly progressive supranuclear palsy

ALTERNATIVE 3: Drug-induced parkinsonism from an unrecognized dopamine-blocking medication
